question: What is GDG ViMEET?
answer: GDG ViMEET is the Google Developer Groups on Campus chapter at Vishwaniketan's Institute of Management, Entrepreneurship and Engineering Technology (ViMEET). It is a student-led developer community where members learn, build and collaborate through workshops, hackathons, study jams and speaker sessions.

question: What does GDG stand for?
variations: What is the full form of GDG?
answer: GDG stands for Google Developer Groups. The full name of this chapter is Google Developer Groups on Campus — ViMEET.

question: What is the GDG ViMEET tagline?
answer: The tagline is "Build. Create. Connect. Go Beyond."

question: Which college is GDG ViMEET part of?
answer: GDG ViMEET is based at Vishwaniketan's Institute of Management, Entrepreneurship and Engineering Technology (ViMEET) in Khalapur, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra - 410210.

question: Do I need to be a programmer to join GDG ViMEET?
variations: I don't know how to code, can I still be part of GDG?
Is this only for computer science students?
answer: No. GDG ViMEET is not only for programmers — the community covers design, content and social media, PR and outreach, event management, entrepreneurship and community building alongside technology. There are teams for each of those.

question: What kind of activities does GDG ViMEET run?
answer: The chapter runs workshops, hackathons, study jams and speaker sessions, with hands-on experience in Web, Mobile, Cloud and AI/ML. Members take part in project-based workshops, team challenges, innovation labs and mentorship programs.

question: What areas does the community cover beyond coding?
variations: What domains do you work in?
What skills can I explore here?
answer: The "Go Beyond Code" areas are Technology, AI, Web & App Development, Cloud, Design, Graphics, Content & Social, PR & Outreach, Events, Entrepreneurship, Community and Innovation.

question: Which academic year is this chapter running for?
answer: The current chapter year is 2026-27. The site also lists the previous tenure, 2025-26, on the Team page.

question: Is GDG ViMEET officially connected to Google?
variations: Is this an official Google club?
answer: GDG ViMEET is a Google Developer Groups on Campus chapter, which is a student community program. The site does not describe any other form of affiliation, so for anything official please email gdgvimeet@gmail.com.

question: Is there a membership fee to join GDG ViMEET?
variations: Do I have to pay to join?
answer: The website does not mention any fee for applying or joining, and the application form does not ask for a payment. If you have been asked to pay something, please confirm with the team at gdgvimeet@gmail.com before paying.

question: What does GDG ViMEET offer its members?
variations: What are the benefits of joining?
What do I get out of being a member?
answer: The recruitment page highlights hands-on project labs, Google mentorship, hackathons and tech talks, and a certificate with GDG swag. Members also get to help organise events rather than only attend them.

question: Who can be part of the GDG ViMEET community?
variations: Is it open to all branches?
answer: It is a student-led community at ViMEET, open to students across branches — the application form lists Computer Engineering, CSE (AIML), Mechanical, EXTC, Civil and Electrical.

question: What is the difference between attending events and joining the core team?
variations: Do I need to join the team to attend events?
Can I come to events without applying?
answer: Events are community activities, while the core team is the group that plans and runs them. As the site puts it: "Don't just attend events. Be part of the team that creates them." Applying through the Join Us page is how you become part of the team.

question: How big is GDG ViMEET?
variations: How many members do you have?
answer: The site does not publish a total membership count. For scale, the Google Cloud Study Jams campaign had 245+ participants, of whom 107 completed it.

question: What technologies does the community focus on?
variations: What tech stack do you work with?
Do you cover AI and cloud?
answer: The focus areas are Web, Mobile, Cloud and AI/ML, delivered through project-based workshops, team challenges, innovation labs and mentorship. Recent activity includes a Google Cloud Study Jams campaign and a Git & GitHub workshop.

question: How do I contact GDG ViMEET?
variations: How can I reach the team?
answer: Email gdgvimeet@gmail.com. You can also reach the chapter on Instagram (@gdgvimeet) or LinkedIn, and the Contact page has a map and contact form.

question: What is the GDG ViMEET Instagram?
answer: The Instagram handle is @gdgvimeet — https://www.instagram.com/gdgvimeet/. Announcements and event highlights are posted there.

question: Is GDG ViMEET on LinkedIn?
variations: Where can I follow you professionally?
answer: Yes — https://www.linkedin.com/company/gdgvimeet/. Campaign recaps, such as the Google Cloud Study Jams write-up, are posted there.

question: Does GDG ViMEET have a GitHub?
answer: Yes — https://github.com/gdgvimeet, linked from the site footer and Contact page.

question: What is the phone number for GDG ViMEET?
answer: No phone number is published on the website. Email gdgvimeet@gmail.com or message the chapter on Instagram instead.

question: Where is ViMEET located?
variations: How do I get to the college?
answer: Vishwaniketan Institute of Management, Entrepreneurship and Engineering Technology, Khalapur, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra - 410210. The Contact page embeds a Google Map of the campus.

question: What kinds of things can I contact GDG ViMEET about?
variations: What do you handle on the contact page?
Can I reach out about a collaboration?
answer: The Contact page lists general questions, collaborations, workshops and talks, community, partnerships and recruitment.

question: How can my company sponsor or partner with GDG ViMEET?
variations: I want to sponsor an event
Can we collaborate with your club?
answer: Partnerships and collaborations are listed as reasons to get in touch — email gdgvimeet@gmail.com. Sponsorship and outreach are handled by the PR & Outreach team.

question: Can I invite GDG ViMEET to speak or run a workshop?
variations: How do I propose a talk?
Can you run a session at my college?
I want to suggest a workshop
answer: Yes — "Workshops & Talks" is one of the listed reasons to reach out, and the Events page has a "Propose a Workshop / Talk" link that emails gdgvimeet@gmail.com.

question: How long does GDG ViMEET take to reply?
variations: When will I get a response?
How fast do you answer emails?
answer: The site does not state a response time. For anything urgent, Instagram direct messages are usually the fastest way to get attention alongside email.

question: Is there a contact form on the website?
variations: Can I message you from the site?
Is there a Google Form to contact you?
answer: The Contact page embeds a Google Form for general enquiries. That form link is still being finalised on the site, so if it does not load, email gdgvimeet@gmail.com instead.

question: Is there a WhatsApp group for GDG ViMEET?
variations: How do I join the WhatsApp community?
answer: Yes — after you submit a recruitment application, the confirmation email includes a "Join WhatsApp Group" button for chapter announcements. The group link is sent by email rather than published on the site.

question: How do I stay updated on upcoming events?
variations: How will I know about the next event?
answer: Follow @gdgvimeet on Instagram and the chapter's LinkedIn page — that is where announcements go. The Events page also lists what is coming up next.

question: Can students from other colleges join or attend?
variations: I'm not a ViMEET student, can I join?
Can I attend if I study elsewhere?
answer: The recruitment form is built for ViMEET students — it asks for a ViMEET roll number and lists ViMEET departments. The site does not say whether outside students can attend events, so please ask at gdgvimeet@gmail.com.

question: Who built the GDG ViMEET website?
answer: The site is built and maintained by the GDG ViMEET Web-Dev team. For anything about the website itself, email gdgvimeet@gmail.com.

question: What pages does this website have?
variations: How do I navigate the site?
answer: There are five public pages: Home, Team, Events, Contact and Join Us (the recruitment form). The navigation bar at the top links to all of them.

question: Where is the application form?
answer: The form is on the Join Us page at /join (also reachable at /recruitment). Every "Apply" button on the site leads there.

question: Where can I see past event photos?
variations: Can I see pictures from your events?
answer: Yes — on the Events page, each past event has a photo stack and a "View Photos" button that opens the full gallery.

question: Where can I read about the club on the site?
answer: There is no separate About page — the About section is part of the Home page. The "About" link in the navigation scrolls you to it.

question: What is on the Team page?
variations: Where can I see the team members?
Who is listed on the team page?
answer: The Team page shows the 2026-27 recruitment teams with an Apply Now button, followed by the previous tenure (2025-26) leadership and team members, and the faculty who guide the chapter.

question: Is there an admin login on this website?
answer: There is an admin area at /admin, but it is only for GDG ViMEET core team members who review applications. Applicants do not need an account — you simply submit the form.

question: Do I need to create an account to apply?
variations: Do I need a login to submit the form?
answer: No account is needed. The recruitment form on /join is open — just fill it in and submit.

question: Does the website work on mobile?
variations: Can I apply from my phone?
answer: Yes. The site is responsive and the recruitment form works on a phone — use the menu button in the top-right to open navigation on mobile.

question: Where do I find the recruitment teams and what they do?
variations: How do I learn about each team?
answer: Both the Team page and the Join Us form list all five teams with a short description of what each one does.

question: Can I filter events by type?
variations: How do I find only workshops?
Is there a way to sort events?
answer: Yes — the Events page has category filters: All, Study Jams, Workshops, Hackathons and Community.

question: Which teams can I apply to at GDG ViMEET?
answer: There are five teams: Technical, Graphics & Design, Content & Social Media, PR & Outreach, and Event Management. You can apply to more than one.

question: What does the Technical team do?
variations: Tell me about the Technical team
What work does the tech team handle?
What happens in the coding team?
answer: The Technical team builds web applications, runs AI/ML and Cloud workshops, and organises competitive hackathons and coding labs. Its badge on the site is "Code & Workshops".

question: What does the Graphics & Design team do?
variations: Tell me about the design team
What does the graphics team work on?
answer: The Graphics & Design team designs official GDG branding, social media posts, UI mockups, event banners and stickers. Its badge is "Design Task Req." because there is an optional poster task with the application.

question: What does the Content & Social Media team do?
variations: Tell me about the content team
Is there a social media role?
answer: The Content & Social Media team creates reels, writes social copy, photographs events and leads community engagement. Its badge is "Media & Reels".

question: What does the PR & Outreach team do?
variations: Tell me about the PR team
answer: The PR & Outreach team drives college sponsorships, connects with campus clubs, manages external outreach and handles media relations. Its badge is "Outreach & Sponsors".

question: What does the Event Management team do?
variations: Tell me about the events team
answer: The Event Management team coordinates hackathons and tech talks, handles logistics, hosts speaker sessions and manages crowds. Its badge is "Operations".

question: Can I apply to more than one team?
variations: Do I have to pick just one team?
How many teams can I choose?
answer: Yes. The form allows multiple selections and says so explicitly: "You can select more than one team if you are interested in multiple domains!" You must select at least one.

question: Which team should I choose?
variations: Which team is right for me?
I don't know which team to apply for
answer: Pick by what you want to spend time on: Technical for building and workshops, Graphics & Design for visual design, Content & Social Media for reels and writing, PR & Outreach for sponsorships and partnerships, Event Management for running events. You can select several if you are torn.

question: Does applying to multiple teams improve my chances?
variations: Is it better to select all teams?
answer: The site does not say that selecting more teams helps. Choose the teams you genuinely want to work in — your motivation answer matters more than the number of boxes ticked.

question: Do I need coding skills for the Technical team?
variations: What skills do I need for the tech team?
Do I need to know programming to join Technical?
What should I know before applying to Technical?
answer: The Technical team works on web applications, AI/ML and Cloud workshops, hackathons and coding labs, so programming interest is expected. The form does not list a required skill level — mention your experience and any projects in the motivation field.

question: What design tools should I know for the Graphics team?
variations: Which software do designers use here?
Do I need Photoshop for the design team?
answer: For the optional poster task the form accepts work made in Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma or Canva — so Canva is fine. Day-to-day work covers branding, social posts, UI mockups, banners and stickers.

question: Do I need video editing skills for the Content team?
variations: What skills does the content team need?
Do I need to make reels?
Is photography part of the content team?
answer: The Content & Social Media team creates reels, writes social copy, photographs events and drives community engagement, so editing, writing or photography skills all fit. Describe what you are strongest at in the motivation field.

question: What skills help for the PR & Outreach team?
variations: Do I need to be good at talking to people for PR?
answer: PR & Outreach is about sponsorships, connecting with campus clubs, external outreach and media relations, so communication and persistence matter more than technical skills.

question: What skills help for the Event Management team?
variations: What does the events team look for?
answer: Event Management covers coordinating hackathons and tech talks, logistics, hosting speaker sessions and crowd management — so organisation, coordination and comfort with people on the day are what count.

question: Is there a web development team?
variations: Can I work on the website?
Is web dev separate from Technical?
answer: For 2026-27 recruitment, web development sits under the Technical team, which handles building web applications. The previous 2025-26 tenure listed a separate Web-Dev team on the Team page.

question: How many people are selected per team?
variations: How many members will you take?
Is there a limit on selections?
answer: The number of seats per team has not been published. Applications are reviewed and shortlisted candidates are invited to an interview round.

question: Can I switch teams after joining?
variations: Is it possible to change my team later?
What if I picked the wrong team?
answer: The website does not describe a process for switching teams after selection. Ask the core team at gdgvimeet@gmail.com — in practice this is usually handled case by case.

question: Which team is best for a first-time applicant with no experience?
variations: I'm a beginner, which team should I join?
Which team is easiest to start with?
I have no experience, can I still apply?
answer: Any of them — the form does not require prior experience, and the motivation field exists so you can explain your interest. Event Management and Content & Social Media are common starting points, but pick what you actually want to learn.

question: Is the Technical team only about web development?
variations: Can I do cloud work in the Technical team?
answer: No — alongside web applications, the Technical team runs AI/ML and Cloud workshops and organises hackathons and coding labs.

question: Do all teams require a task or assignment?
variations: Is there a task for every team?
Do I have to submit work with my application?
answer: No. Only the Graphics & Design team has a task, the Ganesh Chaturthi poster, and even that one is optional and marked as a bonus. Every other team just needs the form.

question: Can I join the Technical team if I only know the basics?
variations: I know a little Python, is that enough?
How good do I need to be at coding?
answer: The site sets no minimum skill bar. The Technical team runs workshops and labs, which means learning is part of the work — explain your current level honestly in the motivation field.

question: What is the time commitment for a team member?
variations: How many hours per week does this take?
Is it a big time commitment?
answer: The website does not state a weekly time commitment. Workload varies around events and campaigns — ask during the interview round or email gdgvimeet@gmail.com.

question: Are team positions paid?
variations: Do core team members get a stipend?
answer: These are student community roles; the site lists benefits like hands-on project labs, mentorship, hackathons and a certificate with GDG swag, not payment.

question: Do I get a certificate for being on a team?
variations: Will I get proof of my role?
answer: Yes — "Certificate & GDG Swag" is listed among the benefits on the recruitment page.

question: Is there a leadership position I can apply for?
variations: Can I apply to be a lead?
How do I become GDG Lead?
answer: The application form is for the five teams and does not include a lead role. The Team page shows that the previous tenure had a GDG Lead and team leads, but the site does not describe how those are appointed — ask at gdgvimeet@gmail.com.

question: What is the difference between the Content team and the Graphics team?
variations: Content vs graphics, which is which?
answer: Graphics & Design makes the visual assets — branding, posters, banners, UI mockups and stickers. Content & Social Media handles reels, written copy, event photography and audience engagement. They work closely but the first is design, the second is media and words.

question: What is the difference between PR & Outreach and Event Management?
variations: Who talks to sponsors and who runs the event?
answer: PR & Outreach works outward — sponsorships, other clubs, media relations. Event Management works on delivery — logistics, hosting, speakers and crowd handling on the day.

question: Can first-year students apply to any team?
variations: Is any team closed to juniors?
Are there year restrictions per team?
answer: No team is restricted by year on the site, but the form's year options are SE, TE and BE — first-year (FE) is not currently selectable. Email gdgvimeet@gmail.com if you are in first year and want to take part.

question: Will I get to work on real projects?
variations: Will I have something to show for it?
answer: Yes — the recruitment page lists hands-on project labs, and teams ship real work: the Technical team builds applications and runs workshops, Graphics produces the chapter's branding, and Events runs hackathons and tech talks.

question: Can I contribute without formally joining a team?
variations: Can I volunteer for one event?
Is there a way to help occasionally?
answer: The site only describes the formal application route for joining a team. If you want to help with a single event, email gdgvimeet@gmail.com and ask — that is not covered on the website.

question: How do I apply to GDG ViMEET?
variations: How do I become a member?
answer: Go to the Join Us page at /join, fill in your student details, pick at least one team, and submit. You will see an Application ID on screen and get a confirmation email.

question: Are applications open right now?
variations: Is it too late to apply?
answer: The recruitment page shows "Applications Open • ViMEET 2026-27" and the form accepts submissions. No closing date is published, so apply as soon as you can and watch @gdgvimeet on Instagram for announcements.

question: What is the deadline to apply?
variations: How long do I have to apply?
answer: No deadline has been announced on the website. Applications are currently open — check @gdgvimeet on Instagram for a closing date announcement.

question: What information do I need to fill in the form?
variations: What fields are in the application?
What details do you ask for?
What should I keep ready before applying?
answer: Full name, roll number, department, year of study, a 10-digit WhatsApp/mobile number, your email, and at least one team. Optionally you can add a short motivation note, and Graphics applicants may add a poster Drive link.

question: Which fields are compulsory?
variations: What is required in the form?
Which fields can I leave blank?
answer: Required: full name, roll number, department, year, mobile number, email, and at least one team. Optional: the motivation note and, for Graphics & Design, the poster Drive link.

question: Which departments can I select?
variations: Is my department in the dropdown?
answer: Computer Engineering, CSE (AIML), Mechanical, EXTC, Civil and Electrical.

question: My department is not in the list — what do I do?
variations: What if my course is missing from the dropdown?
answer: The form only offers Computer Engineering, CSE (AIML), Mechanical, EXTC, Civil and Electrical. If none fits, email gdgvimeet@gmail.com so the team can guide you rather than submitting a wrong branch.

question: Which years of study can apply?
answer: The form offers SE, TE and BE, with SE selected by default.

question: Can first-year (FE) students apply?
variations: I am in first year, can I join?
Why can't I select first year?
answer: The form's year options are only SE, TE and BE, so first year is not currently selectable. If you are in FE and want to take part, email gdgvimeet@gmail.com.

question: What format should my mobile number be in?
variations: Why is my phone number rejected?
What number format does the form accept?
answer: Enter a 10-digit Indian mobile number starting with 6, 7, 8 or 9 — the +91 prefix is already shown, so do not type it. Anything else shows "Please enter a valid 10-digit Indian mobile number."

question: Should I use my college email or personal email?
variations: Do I need a vimeet.ac.in email?
answer: Any valid email works — the field's example shows a college address, but it is not enforced. Use one you actually check, because your confirmation and interview updates go there.

question: What roll number should I enter?
variations: What is the roll number format?
Which roll number do you want?
Does case matter for roll number?
answer: Your college roll number — the form shows "e.g. 23CE045" as the example. It is saved in uppercase automatically, so case does not matter.

question: Is the motivation section compulsory?
variations: Do I have to write why I want to join?
Can I skip the 'Why GDG ViMEET' box?
What should I write in motivation?
answer: It is optional. If you do write something, mention past experience, projects, or why you want to join — you can include GitHub, LinkedIn or portfolio links there.

question: Do I need a Google Drive link to apply for the Graphics team?
variations: Is the poster task compulsory for Graphics & Design?
Can I apply for graphics without submitting a design?
What is the Ganesh Chaturthi poster task?
Do I have to do the design task?
answer: No — the Ganesh Chaturthi poster is an optional bonus task for the Graphics & Design team. You can submit without it, but a Drive link set to "Anyone with the link can view" strengthens your application.

question: How do I submit the poster for the Graphics team?
variations: How do I share my design?
What are the poster submission rules?
How should I upload my artwork?
answer: Design an original Ganesh Chaturthi poster in Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma or Canva, export it as JPG, PNG or PDF, upload it to Google Drive, set sharing to "Anyone with the link can view", then paste that link in the form.

question: Why is my poster link being rejected?
variations: The Drive link shows an error
Invalid URL on the poster field
answer: The link must be a full URL starting with http or https. Paste the complete Google Drive address rather than a shortened or partial one.

question: Can I submit the poster later, after applying?
variations: I forgot to add my design link
Can I send my poster after submitting the form?
answer: The form has no way to add it later. Submit the form anyway and email your Drive link to gdgvimeet@gmail.com with your Application ID.

question: How long does the application take to fill?
answer: It is short — one screen with student details, team selection and an optional motivation box. A few minutes at most, longer only if you are preparing the optional Graphics poster.

question: Can I edit my application after submitting?
variations: I made a mistake in my form
How do I change my details?
answer: There is no edit option once submitted. Email gdgvimeet@gmail.com with your Application ID and the correction, or submit again and mention which entry is the correct one.

question: Can I apply twice?
variations: Can I submit more than one application?
answer: The form does allow another submission — the success screen even has a "Submit Another Response" button. If you are correcting an earlier entry, mention that in the motivation field or email gdgvimeet@gmail.com so the team knows which to keep.

question: What happens right after I submit?
variations: What do I see after applying?
How do I know my form went through?
answer: You get a success screen with your Application ID, department and year, and selected teams, plus a confirmation email. If you see that ID, your application was saved.

question: What is an Application ID and why do I need it?
variations: What is the ID shown after applying?
Should I save my application ID?
What does gdg- mean in my ID?
answer: It is your unique reference, in the form gdg-xxxxxxxx-xxxx. Save it — quoting it in any email about your application makes it much faster for the team to find you.

question: The form won't submit — what should I check?
variations: My application is not going through
I get an error when applying
answer: Check the fields marked in red: a 10-digit mobile starting 6-9, a valid email, name and roll number filled in, and at least one team selected. If everything looks right and it still fails, try again shortly or email gdgvimeet@gmail.com.

question: Do I need to agree to anything when applying?
variations: Will you contact me on WhatsApp?
answer: Yes — the form notes that by submitting you agree to receive interview updates on WhatsApp and email.

question: Who can see the details I submit?
variations: What do you do with my information?
answer: Applications are reviewed by the GDG ViMEET core team through a password-protected admin dashboard. The site does not publish applicant details anywhere public.

question: Is there an interview?
variations: Is there a test after applying?
answer: Yes — shortlisted students are contacted by email or WhatsApp for an interview round. No written test is mentioned.

question: What should I prepare for the interview?
variations: How do I prepare for the GDG interview?
answer: The site does not publish interview details. Being able to talk about why you chose your team and anything you have built or organised before is a sensible starting point.

question: Do I need a portfolio or GitHub to apply?
variations: Do you want to see my past work?
answer: Nothing is required. The optional motivation field is where you can include GitHub, LinkedIn or portfolio links if you have them.

question: Can I apply from my phone?
variations: Does the form work on mobile?
answer: Yes, the form is responsive and works on a phone.

question: Is there an application fee?
answer: The form never asks for payment. If anyone asks you to pay to apply, verify with gdgvimeet@gmail.com first.

question: What is the difference between /join and /recruitment?
variations: Which link should I use to apply?
answer: They are the same page — both addresses open the recruitment form. Use either.

question: Can I choose a team but change my mind before submitting?
variations: How do I unselect a team?
answer: Yes — team selection toggles, so click a selected team again to remove it. The counter shows how many you have chosen.

question: What if I don't select any team?
variations: Can I apply without choosing a team?
answer: You cannot submit without one. The form shows "Please select at least one team you want to join."

question: Do I need to be present on campus to join?
answer: The site does not state an attendance policy. Since events run on campus at ViMEET, expect some in-person involvement — ask during the interview round.

question: I applied last year — do I need to apply again?
variations: I was in the 2025-26 team, what now?
answer: This recruitment is for the 2026-27 chapter and the site lists 2025-26 as the previous tenure, so submit a fresh application. If you were on the previous team, say so in the motivation field.

question: Will I get a confirmation email after applying?
variations: Do you send an email after I apply?
How do I know you received my form?
answer: Yes. You get an email titled "Application Received - GDG Vimeet" listing your Application ID, name, roll number, department, year, mobile and selected teams, plus a button to join the WhatsApp group.

question: I didn't get the confirmation email — what should I do?
variations: Check if my application went through
answer: Check your spam and promotions folders first. If you saw an Application ID on screen after submitting, your application was saved even if the email did not arrive — email gdgvimeet@gmail.com with that ID to confirm.

question: What are the next steps after I apply?
variations: What is the process after applying?
answer: The team reviews your application and any portfolio or poster you submitted. Shortlisted students get an email or WhatsApp update inviting them to the interview round. Announcements are posted on @gdgvimeet on Instagram.

question: How long does it take to hear back?
variations: How many days for a response?
What is the timeline for selection?
answer: No timeline has been published. Watch your email and @gdgvimeet on Instagram for updates.

question: Can I check my application status online?
variations: How do I track my application?
Where can I see if I was selected?
answer: There is no self-service status page — the dashboard that holds statuses is for core team members only. Email gdgvimeet@gmail.com with your Application ID if you need an update.

question: What does my application status mean?
answer: Internally an application moves through Pending Review (the default when submitted), Reviewed, Shortlisted or Rejected. Shortlisted means you are being invited to the interview round.

question: Can you tell me if I have been selected?
variations: What is the status of my form?
answer: I cannot look up individual applications — I have no access to applicant records. The team contacts shortlisted students by email or WhatsApp; for a direct update, email gdgvimeet@gmail.com with your Application ID.

question: How will you contact me?
variations: Will you call or email me?
answer: By email and WhatsApp — the form notes that submitting means you agree to receive interview updates on both. Make sure the number and email you entered are correct.

question: How do I join the WhatsApp group?
variations: How do I get chapter announcements?
answer: The "Join WhatsApp Group" button is in your confirmation email. If you cannot find that email, check spam, then email gdgvimeet@gmail.com with your Application ID.

question: Is joining the WhatsApp group compulsory?
variations: Do I have to join the group?
What is the WhatsApp group for?
answer: The email describes it as the place for important announcements and next steps, so it is strongly encouraged. The site does not say it is mandatory.

question: What if I am not selected?

question: Who is eligible to apply to GDG ViMEET?
